create.title: Owner-complete unmasking of the exact small-square-factor cone
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), N=floor(X), I_M=N intersect [M,B_M), B_M<=2M, C(m)=sum_(hr=m,r odd,r>4h)chi_4(r), and write m=s t^2 uniquely with s squarefree. Let S_N^(<,>) be the exact Round-145 scalar restricted to t<M^(1/4) and |floor(t sqrt(Ns)+1/2)^2-Nst^2|>M^(3/4), and let U_N^< be the identical scalar with that nearest-square mask deleted. The ambient support is the disjoint union of the masked small-t set, its small-t |j|<=M^(3/4) complement, and t>=ceil(M^(1/4)). The second set is a subset of the accepted Round-144 absolute cell owner, including its separate exact-radical channel, while the third is the accepted Round-145 unmasked large-t owner. Hence S_N^(<,>)=U_N^<+O_(epsilon,V)(X^epsilon) and the inherited full cone scalar T_N=U_N^<+O_(epsilon,V)(X^epsilon) after logarithmic block assembly. Only the nearest-square mask is removed; the exact multiplicity-one coefficient, squarefree and coprimality support, parity, character, strict cone, profile, clipped half-open endpoints, fixed centre, and individual positive direction remain. The signed U_N^< scalar is not estimated.
create.next_action: Prove U_N^< <<_(epsilon,V) X^epsilon for the exact unmasked small-t coefficient and every clipped prefix, or produce a further owner-complete signed reduction. The t=1 and D=1 faces and the independent Round-138 cross owner remain mandatory.

create.title: Three-variable Hessian, short-face, source-power, and transform-return obstruction
create.statement_tex: For the exact unmasked small-t scalar, write its inherited multiplicity-one coefficient as kappa_t(d,e) and dyadically take t asymp T, d asymp D, e asymp E, with T^2DE asymp M. The coefficient-envelope weighted price is X^epsilon M^(1/4)/T. The relative-coordinate Hessian of f(t,d,e)=sqrt(N)t sqrt(de) is [[0,1/2,1/2],[1/2,-1/4,1/4],[1/2,1/4,-1/4]], with determinant 1/4, but this algebraic fact is not an estimate for the joint arithmetic coefficient. The exact cone gives D<<sqrt(M), E>>sqrt(M)/T^2; E=1 is empty and fixed bounded E is terminal-safe, while t=1 is a mandatory rank-one d,e face and D=1 is structurally present. A t-difference has a constant h=0 diagonal and rank-one h!=0 phases with unproved exact coefficient correlations. The smooth full stationary phase is -2u sqrt(vw)/sqrt(N); c maps to -2/c and back only at the phase level after alias-orthant reversal, while aliaswise modulus has adverse upper capacity. No audited theorem accepts the literal coefficient. Even granting ideal separation, Cao-Zhai Theorem 6 leaves R^(3/8-5tau/8+epsilon) on the balanced top box, hence R^(1/16+epsilon) at formal tau=1/2; Cao-Zhai Theorem 7 leaves R^(7/8+epsilon), and the stated Robert-Sargos and Sargos-Wu uses leave R^(1/4+epsilon) at that endpoint. These are limitations of displayed upper bounds, not signed lower bounds or a disproof of the target. No strict fixed-power intermediate-t reduction is proved.
create.next_action: Park determinant-only cancellation, arbitrary-coefficient or smooth-tensor substitution, one t-difference without a correlation theorem, direct use of the audited monomial estimates, and transform-followed-by-modulus. Reopen only with a genuinely sign-sensitive theorem for the exact coefficient or transformed coefficient that also owns bounded t and every short face.

update.next_action: Use the Round-146 child equivalence: the exact first-open small-t scalar is target-equivalent to its unmasked version. The cell theorem removes only the accepted |j|<=M^(3/4) window and supplies no thicker smoothing owner.

Pass to the Round-146 unmasked child scalar. Retain both multiplicity-one coefficient parametrizations, strict t<M^(1/4), profile, clipped endpoints, fixed centre, and positive direction; the nearest-square mask is no longer an active amplitude hypothesis.

The nearest-square mask is now removed owner-completely, but the exact joint coefficient, balanced boxes, bounded-t rank-one face, and varying slow frequencies remain. Reopen only with a sign-sensitive exact-coefficient theorem.
The first-open cone scalar is now unmasked but still restricted to t<M^(1/4). Three-variable Hessian and the audited monomial bounds do not control its exact coefficient or bounded-t faces.

The new t-direction has nonzero three-dimensional Hessian only in the interior. The mandatory t=1 face and every nonzero t-difference return the rank-one d,e product phase with an unproved exact coefficient correlation.

The mask may be restored away, but both the completed-Appell route and the full three-variable stationary transform return the same owner or monomial class. Reopen only with a signed coefficient theorem, not another transform followed by modulus.

The first open cone owner is the exact unmasked t<M^(1/4) squarefree-kernel scalar U_N^< with literal coefficient, strict cone, profile, clipped endpoints, fixed centre, and positive direction. Prove it together with the independent Round-138 collar-tail cross owner before claiming lower GAR.

reject.reason: The accepted Round-144 absolute cell owner removes the small-t |j|<=M^(3/4) subset, so the first-open scalar is target-equivalent to its unmasked version.
A Hessian determinant does not control an arbitrary joint coefficient, and the exact arithmetic amplitude is neither smooth nor separated.
The adversarial bounded array e(-f) cancels the phase identically; a valid theorem must use the exact arithmetic signs and correlations.
The t=1 and D=1 faces are mandatory and have owner-sized available capacity, while fixed t leaves the rank-one d,e Hessian.
The h=0 term is diagonal and every h!=0 returned phase is rank one in d,e with an unproved exact coefficient correlation.
The dual phase is the same monomial class at phase level, and aliaswise triangle inequality has adverse upper capacity.
The literal coefficient fails the separated tensor hypothesis, and even ideal separation leaves R^(3/8-5tau/8), including R^(1/16) at formal tau=1/2.
The coefficient classes fail and the audited direct powers or transformed upper ledgers remain polynomially above target.
Every displayed residual and box capacity is only an upper-bound limitation; cancellation in the exact scalar remains possible.
The unmasked signed cone scalar, independent cross owner, direct M1 parents, all M2 owners, endpoint uniformity, M9, bridge, and quarter target remain open.

no_change.reason: Round 146 simplifies one lower-cone amplitude and rejects a mechanism but proves neither that signed scalar, the independent cross owner, nor either direct blockwise M1 parent.
Hard TOP, BAL, and required UNBAL owners were not treated and remain open.
An unmasking equivalence and mechanism no-go for one lower-cone scalar are not an all-owner endpoint theorem.
M9-M1, M9-M2, and endpoint uniformity remain open.
The bridge remains conditional on the complete open M9 hypothesis.
The strongest internally proved global exponent remains one third.
The separately audited external exponent remains (3292+25sqrt(1717))/13762.
The quarter target still lacks the unmasked small-t lower-radial scalar, remaining M1 and M2 owners, endpoint uniformity, M9, and an unconditional final bridge.

round_assessment.reason: Round 146 proves an owner-complete removal of the nearest-square mask from the exact small-t scalar and fully audits the genuinely nonzero three-variable Hessian. It then establishes a precise method no-go: mandatory rank-one short faces, coefficient nonseparability, differencing and phase-level transform return, and an independently checked Cao-Zhai R^(1/16) residual prevent the proposed direct route from reaching target scale. The signed scalar and every downstream theorem remain open.
